title: Ezra Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezra chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezra Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezra Chapter 6.

questions.question: In Ezra 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Darius the king made a decree and a search was made in the house of the rolls
The golden and silver vessels taken by Nebuchadnezzar were to be restored
Tatnai and Shetharboznai were told to stay away
The decree concerning the height and breadth of the house of God
questions.correctAnswer: Darius the king made a decree and a search was made in the house of the rolls
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:1 records that Darius the king made a decree and a search was made in the house of the rolls first in the chapter.

questions.question: Where was the roll with the record concerning the house of God found?
options: At Achmetha, in the palace in the province of the Medes
In the house of the rolls in Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: At Achmetha, in the palace in the province of the Medes
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:2 states that the roll was found at Achmetha, in the palace that is in the province of the Medes.

questions.question: According to the decree in the first year of Cyrus the king, what was the height of the house of God to be?
questions.correctAnswer: Threescore cubits
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:3 states the height of the house of God was to be threescore cubits.

questions.question: What materials were specified for building the house of God?
options: Three rows of great stones and a row of new timber
questions.correctAnswer: Three rows of great stones and a row of new timber
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:4 specifies the building materials as three rows of great stones and a row of new timber.

questions.question: From where were the expenses for building the house of God to be given?
options: From the tribute of the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: Out of the king's house
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:4 says that the expenses were to be given out of the king's house.

questions.question: What was to happen to the golden and silver vessels taken by Nebuchadnezzar?
options: They were to be restored and brought again to the temple in Jerusalem
They were to be melted down
They were to be kept in Babylon
They were to be distributed among the Medes
questions.correctAnswer: They were to be restored and brought again to the temple in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:5 states that the golden and silver vessels taken by Nebuchadnezzar were to be restored and brought again to the temple in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Who was told to be far from the place of the house of God during its rebuilding?
options: Tatnai, Shetharboznai, and the Apharsachites beyond the river
Cyrus the king's officials in Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Tatnai, Shetharboznai, and the Apharsachites beyond the river
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:6 instructs Tatnai, Shetharboznai, and their companions the Apharsachites beyond the river to be far from there.

questions.question: Who was authorized to build the house of God in his place?
options: The governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: The governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:7 states that the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews were to build the house of God in his place.

questions.question: What did Darius decree concerning the expenses for the building of the house of God?
options: Expenses were to be given from the king's goods, from the tribute beyond the river
The Jews must pay all expenses themselves
Expenses were to be paid by the Medes
No expenses were to be given
questions.correctAnswer: Expenses were to be given from the king's goods, from the tribute beyond the river
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:8 declares that expenses were to be given from the king's goods, even from the tribute beyond the river, to avoid hindrance.

questions.question: Which king originally made the decree concerning the house of God at Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Cyrus the king
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:3 states that in the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus made the decree concerning the house of God.

questions.question: In Ezra 6, who were the Apharsachites mentioned alongside Tatnai and Shetharboznai?
questions.correctAnswer: Companions beyond the river
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:6 mentions the Apharsachites as companions beyond the river along with Tatnai and Shetharboznai.

questions.question: True or False: Darius ordered that the work on the house of God should be stopped.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:7 commands to let the work of the house of God alone and allow the governor and elders to build it, so the work was not to be stopped.

questions.question: True or False: The foundations of the house of God were to be strongly laid according to the decree.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:3 specifically says the foundations thereof were to be strongly laid according to the decree.

questions.question: True or False: The decree allowed Tatnai and Shetharboznai to supervise the building of the house of God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:6 instructs Tatnai, Shetharboznai, and their companions to be far from the place of building, so they were not allowed to supervise.

questions.question: True or False: The decree stated that the expenses for rebuilding were to be paid by the Jews alone, without assistance from the king.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:8 states that expenses were to be given from the king's goods, from the tribute beyond the river, so the Jews were not to pay alone.

medium.title: Ezra Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezra Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What offerings are mentioned in Ezra 6:9 that are to be provided for the burnt offerings?
questions.correctAnswer: Young bullocks, rams, and lambs
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:9 specifically lists young bullocks, rams, and lambs as offerings needed for the burnt offerings of the God of heaven.

questions.question: What does Ezra 6:10 promise will happen if sacrifices are offered to the God of heaven?
options: Prayers for the king's life will be made
questions.correctAnswer: Prayers for the king's life will be made
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:10 states that the sacrifices are to be offered so that prayers may be made for the life of the king and his sons.

questions.question: What decree does Darius make regarding anyone who alters his word according to Ezra 6:11?
options: They will be hanged on a tree
questions.correctAnswer: They will be hanged on a tree
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:11 declares that anyone who alters Darius's decree will face severe punishment, including being hanged from a timber pulled down from their house.

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in Ezra 6:12 for those who try to alter or destroy the house of God?
options: They will be destroyed by God
questions.correctAnswer: They will be destroyed by God
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:12 emphasizes that God will destroy all kings and people who attempt to alter or destroy the house of God at Jerusalem.

questions.question: What role does Tatnai play in the events of Ezra 6:13?
options: He is the king of Persia
He is a governor who follows the king's decree
questions.correctAnswer: He is a governor who follows the king's decree
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:13 shows that Tatnai, the governor, and his companions acted according to the decree that Darius had sent, ensuring that the work was done.

questions.question: According to Ezra 6:14, who helped the elders of the Jews prosper in their building efforts?
questions.correctAnswer: The prophets Haggai and Zechariah
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:14 states that the elders of the Jews prospered in rebuilding due to the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah.

questions.question: When was the house finished according to Ezra 6:15?
options: On the first day of the month Adar
On the third day of the month Adar
On the sixth year of Darius's reign
On the tenth day of the month Adar
questions.correctAnswer: On the third day of the month Adar
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:15 mentions that the house was finished on the third day of the month Adar during the sixth year of King Darius's reign.

questions.question: What was the response of the children of Israel during the dedication of the house of God as stated in Ezra 6:16?
questions.correctAnswer: With joy
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:16 indicates that the children of Israel, including the priests and Levites, kept the dedication of the house of God with joy.

questions.question: How did the decree of Darius impact the building of the house of God as seen in Ezra 6:8?
options: It authorized the use of royal funds
questions.correctAnswer: It authorized the use of royal funds
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:8 reveals that Darius's decree allowed for expenses to be given from the king's goods to ensure the building of the house of God was not hindered.

questions.question: What connection can be made between the sacrifices mentioned in Ezra 6:10 and the prosperity mentioned in Ezra 6:14?
options: Sacrifices are not related to prosperity
Prosperity is only for the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Sacrifices lead to prosperity
questions.explanation: The connection shows that offering sacrifices to God leads to His favor, contributing to the prosperity of the elders in rebuilding, as seen in Ezra 6:10 and Ezra 6:14.

questions.question: What assurance does Ezra 6:12 provide regarding the protection of the house of God?
options: God will protect it from destruction
It will be rebuilt by humans
questions.correctAnswer: God will protect it from destruction
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:12 assures that God will destroy those who attempt to alter or destroy His house, indicating His protection over it.

questions.question: The decree made by Darius was to be done with what, according to Ezra 6:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Speed
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:12 mentions that Darius decreed that the work should be done with speed, emphasizing the urgency of the task.

questions.question: Is it true that the house of God was built without the support of the king's decree?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The statement is false; the house of God was built with the support and decree of King Darius, as indicated throughout the chapter.

questions.question: Is it true that Ezra 6:14 states the elders prospered through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This statement is true; Ezra 6:14 credits the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah for the prosperity of the elders in their building efforts.

questions.question: Is it true that Ezra 6:9 mentions the need for gold and silver for the burnt offerings?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: This statement is false; Ezra 6:9 specifically lists young bullocks, rams, and lambs, but does not mention gold or silver for burnt offerings.

hard.title: Ezra Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezra Chapter 6.

questions.question: At the dedication of the house of God, how many lambs were offered according to Ezra 6:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Four hundred lambs
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:17 states that four hundred lambs were offered at the dedication of the house of God.

questions.question: According to Ezra 6:18, how were the priests and Levites organized for service in Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: In divisions and courses
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:18 says the priests were set in their divisions and the Levites in their courses for the service of God in Jerusalem.

questions.question: When did the children of the captivity keep the Passover according to Ezra 6:19?
options: On the fourteenth day of the first month
On the tenth day of the first month
On the first day of the seventh month
questions.correctAnswer: On the fourteenth day of the first month
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:19 specifies that the children of the captivity kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.

questions.question: Who were purified together to kill the Passover according to Ezra 6:20?
questions.correctAnswer: Priests and Levites
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:20 states that priests and Levites were purified together and killed the Passover for all the children of the captivity.

questions.question: According to Ezra 6:21, who joined the children of Israel in eating after the captivity?
options: Those who had separated themselves from the filthiness of the heathen
questions.correctAnswer: Those who had separated themselves from the filthiness of the heathen
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:21 mentions that all who had separated themselves from the filthiness of the heathen joined the children of Israel in eating.

questions.question: For how many days did the children of Israel keep the feast of unleavened bread with joy according to Ezra 6:22?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:22 says they kept the feast of unleavened bread for seven days with joy.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Azazel' (scapegoat) related to sin offerings, as referenced in contexts like Ezra 6:17, mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Complete removal
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term related to sin offerings like the he goats in Ezra 6:17 is often connected to 'Azazel', meaning 'complete removal' of sin, symbolizing the removal of guilt.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently employed in Ezra 6:17-22, where the dedication sacrifice parallels the Passover and feast of unleavened bread?
questions.correctAnswer: Typology
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:17-22 uses typology as the dedication sacrifices and the celebration of Passover foreshadow and parallel later redemptive events.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects to the theme of purification and sacrifice found in Ezra 6:20?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 10:22
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:22 speaks about being purified and having hearts sprinkled, connecting to the purification of priests and Levites in Ezra 6:20.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage fulfills the practice of observing the Passover as seen in Ezra 6:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 12:6
questions.explanation: Exodus 12:6 commands the keeping of the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, directly connecting to Ezra 6:19.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the dedication sacrifices described in Ezra 6:17?
options: The completion of the house of God
The decree of Darius to rebuild the temple
The purification of priests and Levites
questions.correctAnswer: The completion of the house of God
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:15-16 describes the finishing of the house of God and the joyful dedication, which precedes the sacrifices in 6:17.

questions.question: What is the significance of the number twelve in the sin offering of twelve he goats in Ezra 6:17?
options: It represents the twelve tribes of Israel
It symbolizes the twelve months of the year
It denotes twelve days of cleansing
It refers to twelve priests present
questions.correctAnswer: It represents the twelve tribes of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:17 explicitly states the twelve he goats were according to the number of the tribes of Israel, symbolizing all Israel.

questions.question: How does Ezra 6:22 illustrate divine intervention in the rebuilding of the temple?
options: The LORD turned the heart of the king of Assyria to strengthen their hands
God sent an angel to guide the builders
The heavens opened and rain fell abundantly
A prophet appeared to command the work
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD turned the heart of the king of Assyria to strengthen their hands
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:22 states that the LORD made them joyful and turned the heart of the king of Assyria to strengthen their hands in building the house of God.

questions.question: Which type of parallelism is found in Ezra 6:17 with the listing of bullocks, rams, and lambs?
questions.correctAnswer: Climactic parallelism
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:17 uses climactic parallelism, where the list of animals (bullocks, rams, lambs) increases in number and intensity for emphasis.

questions.question: How does the organization of priests and Levites in Ezra 6:18 reflect Mosaic Law?
options: It follows the divisions and courses prescribed in the book of Moses
It is based on new Persian administrative rules
It is arranged by popular vote among Levites
It is determined by age hierarchy rather than lineage
questions.correctAnswer: It follows the divisions and courses prescribed in the book of Moses
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:18 states that the priests and Levites were set in their divisions and courses as written in the book of Moses, reflecting Mosaic Law.

theological.title: Ezra Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezra Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezra 6:3 teach about God's providence in the rebuilding of the temple?
options: God sovereignly ordains the restoration of His worship
Human effort alone ensures the temple's completion
The temple's reconstruction is contingent on political alliances
God's presence is limited to the physical temple
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly ordains the restoration of His worship
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:3 reveals that King Cyrus made a decree for the temple to be rebuilt, demonstrating God's providential orchestration of political powers to fulfill His redemptive purposes.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification is taught in Ezra 6:20 regarding the priests and Levites?
options: Sanctification involves both communal and individual purity before God
Sanctification is only symbolic and not required for temple service
Only the Levites require sanctification, not the priests
Sanctification is unnecessary due to God’s grace alone
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves both communal and individual purity before God
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:20 states that the priests and Levites were purified together to properly perform the Passover, underscoring the necessity of holiness in corporate worship.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment is taught in Ezra 6:12?
options: God executes judgment on those who oppose His temple
God is indifferent to those who alter His decrees
Only earthly kings judge temple matters
questions.correctAnswer: God executes judgment on those who oppose His temple
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:12 pronounces that God will destroy all who alter or destroy the temple, affirming divine judgment against opposition to God's covenant purposes.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezra 6:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:11 shows the king’s decree of severe punishment for altering the temple decree, reflecting God's attribute of justice in upholding His covenant word.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezra 6:10 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:10 calls for continual offerings and prayers for the king, demonstrating God’s faithfulness in maintaining His covenant relationship with His people and their rulers.

questions.question: How does Ezra 6:15 connect to the broader biblical theme of covenant restoration?
options: It fulfills the promise of restoration seen in the Prophets
It marks the end of Israel’s covenant responsibilities
It shows human failure in covenant obedience
It inaugurates a new covenant replacing the old
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the promise of restoration seen in the Prophets
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:15 records the completion of the temple rebuilding, fulfilling prophetic promises of restoration and renewal of Israel’s covenant worship (cf. Isaiah 44:28).

questions.question: How does Ezra 6:17 relate redemptive history by its mention of offering a sin offering for all Israel?
options: It anticipates the ultimate atonement by Christ for Israel’s sin
It replaces the need for future sacrifices
It denies the need for repentance
It limits atonement to the Levitical priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the ultimate atonement by Christ for Israel’s sin
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:17 describes sin offerings for Israel, pointing forward to Christ’s once-for-all atonement that fulfills the sacrificial system (Hebrews 10:1-18).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezra 6:4 and Ezra 6:8 teach about God's provision for His temple and people?
options: God provides materially through earthly authorities for His worship
God’s provision is limited to spiritual blessings only
Believers must provide for themselves without reliance on government
Provision for worship is not necessary for God’s blessing
questions.correctAnswer: God provides materially through earthly authorities for His worship
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:4 commands expenses from the king’s house, and 6:8 orders tribute to be given for temple workers, showing God’s providential use of rulers to supply material needs for worship.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezra 6:16 and Ezra 6:22 teach about joy in covenant worship?
options: Joy is a proper response to God’s faithfulness in covenant restoration
Joy is irrelevant to true worship
Joy depends on human achievement, not divine grace
Joy is only for individual believers, not corporate gatherings
questions.correctAnswer: Joy is a proper response to God’s faithfulness in covenant restoration
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:16 describes the joyful dedication of the temple, and 6:22 explains the joy arising from the LORD’s work and His strengthening, emphasizing joy as a response to God’s covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezra 6:5 and Ezra 6:21 teach about restoration and separation from sin?
options: Restoration includes returning sacred objects and separating from heathen impurity
Restoration is merely political without spiritual implications
Separation from sin is unnecessary for restoration
Restoration focuses solely on physical rebuilding
questions.correctAnswer: Restoration includes returning sacred objects and separating from heathen impurity
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:5 commands restoration of temple vessels, and 6:21 notes separation from heathen filth, teaching that restoration involves both physical and spiritual cleansing.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Ezra 6:11–12 reveals a harsh, vengeful God who imposes brutal punishments arbitrarily. What does Ezra 6:11–12 actually teach?
options: God’s justice upholds His covenant and law with solemn consequences
God is indifferent to temple desecration
God’s punishments are intended only for political control
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice upholds His covenant and law with solemn consequences
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:11–12 show that the punishment for altering the temple decree is severe because it threatens God's covenantal order, emphasizing His righteous justice rather than arbitrary cruelty.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezra 6:9 teach about God’s provision for worship and the role of the priesthood?
options: God ordains continual provision for sacrifices through human agents
Worship does not require material provisions
Sacrifices are obsolete and symbolic only
The priesthood is unnecessary for worship
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains continual provision for sacrifices through human agents
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:9 commands daily provision of animals and offerings according to priestly appointments, indicating God’s order for sustained sacrificial worship via the priesthood.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezra 6:13 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:13 describes officials obeying the king’s decree speedily, illustrating God’s sovereign control over earthly powers to accomplish His purposes.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezra 6:14 and Ezra 6:15 teach about prophetic fulfillment and divine command?
options: The temple’s completion fulfills prophetic word and divine decree
Prophecy has no connection to temple construction
Divine commands are optional in building the temple
questions.correctAnswer: The temple’s completion fulfills prophetic word and divine decree
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:14 credits prophecy of Haggai and Zechariah, and 6:15 records the temple finished by divine command, showing fulfillment of God’s revealed will through prophecy and decree.

questions.question: How does Ezra 6:18 connect to the broader biblical theme of covenant worship and Levitical order?
options: It affirms the continuation of Mosaic priestly divisions for proper worship
It introduces a new priesthood unrelated to Moses
It disregards temple order in worship
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms the continuation of Mosaic priestly divisions for proper worship
questions.explanation: Ezra 6:18 assigns priests and Levites to their courses according to Moses’ book, emphasizing continuity of covenant worship practices.
